narrative:
The Salt Road is quiet in the particular way a place becomes quiet after deciding it has survived. A cooper is fitting a new hoop around a cracked barrel. Two children are trying to ring the broken bell with a spoon. Nobody stops them.

At the inn, three messages wait on the same table: Yeva Solt's precise account of the winter stores, Petra Voss's unsigned note asking whether victory ever feels less lonely, and Tamsin's rumor that the Northern Reach has begun buying black cloth by the mile.

For one evening, no one needs you to save anything. The road only asks what you will carry from it.
